title: Matching size through adjacency-list queries
coverage: Eleven scoped entries from six primary sources, covering the five existing adjacency-list settings; three parameterized related results are retained for inspection. This is a curated comparison, not an exhaustive survey.
defaultScope: Global maximum-cardinality matching size estimates through degree and indexed-neighbor access. Adaptive simple graphs, bipartite graphs, additive error, and non-adaptive queries have separate contracts.

comparisonContracts: Every cost is the total cost of one global size estimate. LCA costs per requested matching edge or vertex and LOCAL communication rounds belong in their own views.
Rows are symbolic resource families; their separation is not a numerical axis or a claim that unknown exponent savings are equal.
BKS and BRR approach 2/3 using different parameter conventions. Neither marker means an exact 2/3 algorithm.
The bipartite lower bound applies to all fixed improvements above 2/3; its upper bound establishes some positive improvement.
For the additive lower bound, δ is chosen first and ε depends on it.
The non-adaptive lower bound uses multigraphs. Its transfer to simple graphs is unproved in the source.
The fixed-tree probe model is omitted as requested.

exclusions.topic: Near-optimal additive size upper bound from Dynamic (1+ε)-Approximate Matching Size in Truly Sublinear Update Time
exclusions.reason: The theorem is stated for adjacency-matrix access. BRR24 footnote 2 describes its adjacency-list extension as believed, not proved; it is not promoted to this figure.
